Work down this page before asking for help. Most problems are on it.

## The first thing to try

**Runtime** {{< fa arrow-right >}} **Restart session and run all**.

A notebook remembers everything you have ever run, including cells you have since
edited or deleted. Restarting clears that memory and runs your cells in the order
they appear. If the error survives a restart, it is a real error.

## Colab problems

### My variables disappeared

The runtime disconnected. Colab reclaims idle notebooks. Your code is untouched.
Run your cells again from the top.

### It says I cannot save

You opened someone else's notebook. **File** {{< fa arrow-right >}} **Save a copy
in Drive**, then work in your copy.

### `torch.cuda.is_available()` returns False

Colab did not give you a GPU. Check **Runtime** {{< fa arrow-right >}} **Change
runtime type** is set to a GPU accelerator. If it is, the free tier is simply out
of GPUs right now. Everything we do runs without one.

### The install cell asks me to restart

Only the `ISLP` package does this, and we do not require it. The November install
cell for `pytorch-lightning` does not.

## Python errors

### `NameError: name 'Auto' is not defined`

The cell that created `Auto` has not run in this session. Run from the top.

### `KeyError: 'Balance'`

No column by that name. Check the spelling, including capitals:

::: {#2c927f72 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import pandas as pd
DATA = "https://lucymcgowan.github.io/sta-363-f26/data/"
Credit = pd.read_csv(DATA + "Credit.csv")
list(Credit.columns)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1}
```
['ID',
 'Income',
 'Limit',
 'Rating',
 'Cards',
 'Age',
 'Education',
 'Gender',
 'Student',
 'Married',
 'Ethnicity',
 'Balance']
```
:::
:::


### `ValueError: Expected 2D array, got 1D array instead`

scikit-learn wants the predictors as a data frame with columns, even when there
is only one.

::: {#444523ed .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
X = Auto["horsepower"]      # wrong, this is one dimensional
X = Auto[["horsepower"]]    # right, note the double brackets
```
:::


### `ValueError: could not convert string to float`

A text column reached a model that only takes numbers. Either drop it or encode
it:

::: {#ecffaf75 .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
y = (Credit["Student"] == "Yes").astype(int)
```
:::


### `ValueError: Input contains NaN`

Missing values. `Hitters` has 59 missing salaries. Either put a `SimpleImputer`
in your pipeline or drop the rows with `.dropna()`.

### `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ISLP'`

You do not need it. Read the CSV instead, as on the [Course Data](data.qmd) page.

### `HTTPError` or `URLError` when reading data

Check the URL for typos and check you are online. The address is exactly:

```
https://lucymcgowan.github.io/sta-363-f26/data/
```

### `SettingWithCopyWarning`

You changed a slice of a data frame rather than the frame. Add `.copy()` when
you subset something you plan to modify.

## Results that look wrong

### My accuracy is suspiciously high

Suspect leakage before you celebrate. Did any preprocessing step see the test
data? Is a predictor recorded after the outcome? This is what the September 11
class is about.

### My numbers changed since last time

You did not set a seed. Add `random_state=363` to `train_test_split`, `KFold`,
and any model with randomness in it.

### My plot did not appear

End the cell with `plt.show()`.

### The model fits but predicts one class for everyone

Common with a rare outcome. Check the class balance with
`y.value_counts(normalize=True)`. Accuracy is a poor measure here, which is the
October 2 class.

## Asking for help

Include these four things and you will get an answer much faster:

1. What you were trying to do  
2. The code you ran, as text rather than a screenshot  
3. The full error message, including the last few lines  
4. What you already tried  

Post in the course discussion so classmates hitting the same wall can see the
answer. See [Help](help.qmd) for office hours and the Math & Stats Center.
